verdict.oneLiner: Easy to create and install in your own workspace. Other workspaces need public distribution, and unlisted commercial apps get heavily rate-limited message history.

approvalWait.note: Unlisted public distribution needs no review. Listing in the Slack Marketplace (recommended for commercial apps) is reviewed; Slack publishes no timeline.

prerequisites.label: A Slack workspace that will own the app
prerequisites.detail: Until you enable distribution the app can only be installed on the workspace that owns it.

prerequisites.label: HTTPS endpoints
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS and can't contain '#'. To distribute, all OAuth, interaction, options-load and Events API URLs must support SSL.

steps.title: Create the app and note its credentials
steps.body: Create the app, then find the client ID, scopes and Redirect URLs on its App Management page.

steps.title: Choose bot and user scopes
steps.body: Bot scopes go in the scope parameter; user scopes go in user_scope and come back under authed_user. Sign in with Slack scopes need their own flow.
steps.agentCanHelp: Picks the minimum bot/user scopes for your features.

steps.title: Add HTTPS redirect URLs
steps.body: The redirect_uri must use HTTPS, must not contain '#', and must match or be a subdirectory of a configured Redirect URL.

steps.title: Implement OAuth v2
steps.body: Send users to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize and exchange the code with oauth.v2.access. Check team.id or enterprise.id in the response rather than trusting the team hint.
steps.agentCanHelp: Writes the install flow and per-workspace token storage.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.body: Complete the distribution checklist to get an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL. Without it, installs on other workspaces fail with invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace (commercial apps)
steps.body: Marketplace apps are reviewed against Slack's requirements and guidelines. Unlisted commercial apps keep working but get reduced rate limits on message history.

scopes.name: channels:history
scopes.note: Reads channel messages via conversations.history, which is throttled for new unlisted commercial apps.

scopes.name: chat:write
scopes.note: Post messages as the bot. Review applies to Marketplace listing, not individual scopes, as far as our sources say.

nuances.title: Tokens don't expire unless you opt into rotation
nuances.body: Bot (xoxb-) and user (xoxp-) tokens don't expire and can only be revoked. With token rotation you get a refresh token and an expiring access token.

nuances.title: Unlisted commercial apps: 1 request/minute on history
nuances.body: Since 29 May 2025, new commercially distributed apps outside the Marketplace, and new installations of existing ones, get Tier 1 limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies: 1 request per minute, max 15 objects. Marketplace apps, internal apps and existing installations are not affected.

nuances.title: Published apps can't add unreviewed scopes
nuances.body: Requesting scopes that are still under review or were never submitted returns unapproved_scope.

blockers.title: invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app
blockers.fix: Activate public distribution for the app.

blockers.title: Reading message history is extremely slow
blockers.symptom: conversations.history returns at most 15 messages and you hit rate limits at 1 request/minute.
blockers.fix: Get listed in the Slack Marketplace, or build as an internal app for a single customer.

blockers.title: Redirect URL rejected
blockers.fix: Use an HTTPS redirect URL without '#' that matches a configured Redirect URL.

agentCan: Choose minimal bot and user scopes
Write the OAuth v2 install flow
Store tokens per workspace and enterprise
humanMust: Create the app and set redirect URLs

unknowns: Active setup time (20–60 min) is our estimate. Not yet checked hands-on.
Slack does not publish a Marketplace review timeline in the pages we read.
Whether localhost redirect URLs are allowed isn't stated; HTTPS is required.
